report.tagline: India's biggest app for booking movie tickets, concerts, comedy shows, plays and sports events.
report.simpleSummary: BookMyShow is the app most Indians use to book a movie seat. You pick a film, a cinema, a time and a seat, pay online, and show a QR code at the door. It also sells tickets for concerts like Coldplay, comedy shows and cricket matches, and it now organises many of those events itself. It earns a small fee on each ticket, plus money from ads and from running live events.

overview.whatItDoes: BookMyShow sells tickets for movies and live events in India. Cinemas list their shows and seats on it, and users book and pay in the app. It also produces and promotes its own events, such as Lollapalooza India, and was the official ticket seller for Coldplay's 2025 India tour.
howItWorks: Cinemas like PVR INOX and single screens connect their seat systems to BookMyShow.
Users choose a movie, cinema, time and seat, then pay with UPI, card or wallet.
BookMyShow adds a convenience fee per ticket and sends an M-ticket with a QR code.
Concert and event organisers list on BookMyShow, or BookMyShow Live runs the event itself and keeps the event profit.
Studios and brands pay to advertise films and products inside the app.
For huge events, it uses online queues and per-user ticket limits to handle millions of buyers at once.
overview.valueProposition: For users: see every show near you, pick your exact seat and skip the queue. For cinemas and organisers: reach most of India's ticket buyers in one place.

businessModel.summary: BookMyShow makes money from four things: a convenience fee on each ticket, a commission from cinemas and organisers, running its own live events, and ads.

revenueStreams.detail: Charged to the user on each ticket, often ₹20 to ₹50 plus GST for movies.
A share of ticket value, higher for events than movies.
Producing and promoting events like Lollapalooza India; income from tickets, sponsors and food. ₹756 crore in FY25.
Film trailers, banners and sponsored listings paid by studios and brands.
Food pre-orders, ticket cancellation cover, gift cards.

businessModel.pricing: Free for users to browse. Convenience fee per ticket shown at checkout, usually ₹20 to ₹60 per movie ticket including GST. Event fees vary by event.
costDrivers: Artist fees and production costs for live events
Marketing, raised in FY25 partly to fight Zomato's District
Tech for seat sync and handling huge traffic spikes
Cashback and offer costs not covered by banks
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a ₹300 movie ticket, the user pays about ₹30 to ₹40 extra as a convenience fee. After GST and a payment charge of about 2%, BookMyShow keeps perhaps ₹20 to ₹25 per ticket. A booking of two seats earns it about ₹40 to ₹50. Live events are bigger bets: on a ₹5,000 concert ticket it may keep several hundred rupees as fees, and if it produces the show it keeps the event profit but also carries the risk of artist fees and low sales. These are rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Being the default place to book a movie, so search and word of mouth bring users
Exclusive ticketing rights for huge events like Coldplay and big cricket matches
Bank and card partnerships with discounts
Ads, raised by about 21% in FY25
whatBringsUsersBack: Alerts when bookings open for a favourite star or artist
Saved payment and city settings that make the next booking faster
growth.moat: Almost every cinema in India, big and small, is connected to BookMyShow, and most users already have the app. That two-sided network is hard to copy. Exclusive deals with big artists and its own festivals add to it.

competitors.name: District by Zomato (Eternal)
competitors.positioning: Going-out app for movies, events and dining, built from Paytm Insider and Zomato Live.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: District has Zomato's user base and dining tie-ins. BookMyShow has more cinemas and longer ties with organisers.

competitors.name: PVR INOX app
competitors.positioning: India's biggest multiplex chain selling directly.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: PVR can skip aggregator fees. BookMyShow shows all cinemas in one place.

competitors.name: Paytm movies
competitors.positioning: Movie tickets inside the Paytm payments app.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Paytm uses cashback; BookMyShow has broader event supply.

competitors.name: Ticketmaster (global)
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Not big in India yet, but the template BookMyShow copies for live events and dynamic pricing.

strengths: Near-default app for movie booking in India, with most cinemas connected
Profitable, with ₹192 crore net profit in FY25
Strong live events business with its own festivals
weaknesses: Site crashes and scalping during big drops hurt trust
Movie ticketing growth is slow, about 12% in FY25
Depends on Bollywood and regional box office hits
risks: District by Zomato spending to win users and artists
Multiplex chains pushing users to their own apps
State rules that cap ticket prices or fees, such as moves in Karnataka in 2025
Police cases and public anger if a big sale goes badly
userComplaints: Website and app crashed when Coldplay Mumbai tickets went on sale in 2024, with fans stuck in queues

improvementIdeas.idea: Official fan-to-fan resale at face value, inside BookMyShow
improvementIdeas.problem: Scalpers resell concert tickets at huge markups and fans get scammed.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Less fraud, more trust, and a small fee earned on each resale.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of resold tickets that go through the official resale

improvementIdeas.idea: Verified-fan lottery for mega concerts instead of first-come queues
improvementIdeas.problem: Bots and crashes make big drops feel unfair.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer crashes and fewer bot purchases.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Big-drop success rate and checkout error rate

improvementIdeas.idea: A yearly 'no convenience fee' membership for about ₹499
improvementIdeas.problem: Fees annoy frequent moviegoers and push them to cinema apps.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Lock in heavy users and steady income.

improvementIdeas.idea: Weekday deals for single screens in tier-2 cities
improvementIdeas.problem: Small cinemas have empty weekday seats.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More tickets used and happier cinema partners.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Weekday occupancy at partner single screens

pmLessons: A marketplace with both sides locked in, cinemas and viewers, is hard to beat, even by a rich rival like Zomato.
Peak moments decide brand trust. One crashed concert sale gets more news than a million smooth movie bookings.
Adding your own supply, like producing live events, can grow revenue faster but adds real risk.
Fees users can see at checkout get the most complaints, so explain or bundle them.

interviewQuestions.question: Coldplay tickets go on sale and 1 crore users show up for 1.5 lakh seats. How would you design the sale?
interviewQuestions.hint: Set goals: fairness, no crash, no bots. Options: lottery, verified fans, queues, ID-linked tickets. Pick one and name metrics like checkout error rate.

interviewQuestions.question: District is spending heavily to take share. How should BookMyShow respond?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find where District is strong (dining, Zomato users). Defend core (cinemas, exclusives), match on fees where it matters, avoid a cash war.

interviewQuestions.question: What is BookMyShow's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Tickets used, not app downloads. Break into bookers, bookings per user, tickets per booking.

interviewQuestions.question: Should BookMyShow remove the convenience fee?
interviewQuestions.hint: Calculate how much income it brings, test a membership, watch effect on cinema apps and margins.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow weekday movie bookings?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users (students, retirees), price deals with cinemas, use alerts. Track weekday occupancy.
